annotations.target_phrase: the geodesic domes enclosing BAMA, climate-controlled synthetic sky
annotations.annotation_text: The geodesic dome architecture of BAMA (Boston-Atlanta Metropolitan Axis) reflects the influence of Buckminster Fuller's techno-utopian design repurposed into late-capitalist environmental management. The synthetic sky provides continuous artificial twilight, isolating citizens from ecological reality.
sources: Brians, Paul. Study Guide for William Gibson: Neuromancer (1984). WSU.
Jameson, Fredric. Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism. Duke UP, 1991.

annotations.annotation_text: Sprawl housing consists of 'conapts' (condominium apartments), mass-produced modular units stacked into vertical megastructures. Gibson borrows the term from Philip K. Dick, highlighting the dystopian continuum of mid-to-late twentieth-century speculative urbanism.
sources: Raubenweiss, Anton. The Sprawl Lexicon. The William Gibson Aleph.
